clue.text: It never fails to spot its victim

definitions.text: It never fails to spot its victim

parts.words: It never fails to spot its victim
parts.note: reads like praise for a sharp-eyed hunter, but 'spot' means cover with red spots: a childhood illness that always leaves its rash

explanation.surface: A predator that never misses its quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' looks like 'notice' but means 'mark with spots'; the illness always brings out its rash on the sufferer.
explanation.definitionFit: This viral infection is known for covering the patient in a red spotty rash.

clue.text: One of them was cracked by the Shalott curse

definitions.text: One of them was cracked by the Shalott curse

parts.words: One of them was cracked by the Shalott curse
parts.note: in Tennyson's poem the Lady of Shalott sees the world only in a glass, which cracks from side to side when the curse falls

explanation.surface: Something broken by the curse in Tennyson's poem.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'The Lady of Shalott' the line 'The mirror crack'd from side to side' marks the curse coming upon her.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking glasses; the Lady's glass split when she turned to look at Lancelot.

clue.text: They hope 'to rebuild Paris with support of workers

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece goes underneath, so it comes last
rebuilding the city puts its letters back together in a new order

parts.note: worker ants are the standard crossword workers

explanation.surface: Volunteers dream of reconstructing the French capital with labourers' help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rebuild' rearranges PARIS as ASPIR; 'with support of' puts ANTS beneath it in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopefuls aspire to something, so they are people who hope.

clue.text: It takes a lot more than this weapon to, make a knight

definitions.text: It takes a lot more than this weapon to, make a knight

parts.words: It takes a lot more than this weapon to, make a knight
parts.note: a knight of the Round Table is named by adding 'a lot' to this weapon's name

explanation.surface: Being armed with a spear does not make you a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: Add LOT to this weapon and you get Lancelot, the Arthurian knight.
explanation.definitionFit: A long spear carried by mounted knights; plus LOT it names Arthur's knight.

clue.text: No doubt he held a copyright in his work

definitions.text: No doubt he held a copyright in his work

parts.words: No doubt he held a copyright in his work
parts.note: 'copyright' read as copy-right: a clerk whose job was to copy documents correctly

explanation.surface: An author who surely owned the rights to his writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copyright' suggests ownership of a text, but read as 'copy right' it describes a professional copyist of documents.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerk who copied out documents by hand before printing and typing.

clue.text: Midland town in need of a hair-dresser ?

definitions.meaning: a spa town in Derbyshire, in the English Midlands
split as two words, a matted tress of hair, which badly wants combing out

explanation.surface: A provincial town so scruffy it could do with a barber.
explanation.walkthrough: Matlock is a Derbyshire spa town; split in two it is a tangled (matted) lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derbyshire town is in England's Midlands; a tangled tress certainly wants a stylist's attention.

clue.text: Tiny tots offered by widows

definitions.meaning: in the Gospel a poor widow gives two small coins, the widow's mite

explanation.surface: Small children handed over by bereaved women.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible a poor widow gives her two small coins, the 'widow's mite'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny arachnids or little children, and the small coins of the biblical widow's gift.

clue.text: A topping cottage industry, theirs

parts.note: 'topping' means excellent but here it is roofing: craftsmen who put straw roofs on cottages

explanation.surface: A splendid home-based trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' looks like 'excellent', but here it is putting a top on a cottage: straw or reed roofing.
explanation.definitionFit: Craftsmen who roof cottages with straw or reed.

clue.text: Marmion's last words to Stanley about one vegetable

indicators.note: the dying knight's call goes round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: in Scott's poem Marmion dies crying 'Charge, Chester, charge! On, Stanley, on!'
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A dying hero's final shout concerns a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: Scott's Marmion dies crying 'On, Stanley, on!'; the urgings ON ON go about I.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulb vegetable with a pungent taste used in cooking.

clue.text: Where a housewife gets to know about irritation

indicators.note: the word for knowing goes around the other piece

parts.note: ken is to know, in Scots and old English
an itch is an irritation of the skin

explanation.surface: A homemaker discovering an annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: KEN (to know, a Scots word) goes about ITCH; 'gets' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: The room where cooking is done, the traditional domain of a housewife.

clue.text: Tearaway city

definitions.meaning: read as a verb phrase, to tear away is to rush on
a cathedral city in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A rowdy youngster from the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tearaway' looks like a noun for a hooligan, but it is read as the phrase 'rip on', to tear off at speed. Ripon is a small cathedral city in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: To rip on is to tear onward; the Yorkshire place has city status thanks to its cathedral.

clue.text: An MC ?

parts.note: MC suggests a compere or Military Cross, but read as Master of Ceremonies in church: someone devoted to the forms of worship

explanation.surface: A compere at a show.
explanation.walkthrough: MC usually suggests a compere, but here it is a 'master of ceremonies' in the religious sense: someone keen on ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who insists on ceremonial forms is literally a master of ceremonies.

clue.text: Wherein we underlings must seek our' fault, said Cassius

definitions.text: Wherein we underlings must seek our' fault, said Cassius

parts.words: Wherein we underlings must seek our' fault, said Cassius
parts.note: Shakespeare's Cassius tells Brutus the fault is not in our stars but in us, that we are underlings

explanation.surface: A quotation from Julius Caesar about where blame lies.
explanation.walkthrough: In Julius Caesar Cassius says 'The fault, dear Brutus, is not in our stars, but in ourselves, that we are underlings.'
explanation.definitionFit: Cassius locates blame within us rather than in fate or the stars.

clue.text: A bind for a horse — that is a certainty

definitions.meaning: a saddle girth that binds the saddle onto a horse
informally, a sure thing or easy task

explanation.surface: Strapping a horse's saddle on firmly is a sure thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a saddle girth strap and, colloquially, a sure thing.

clue.text: Goes down in 8s

definitions.meaning: 8 is the kitchen (8-down): washing basins are found in kitchens

explanation.surface: Something drops several times over.
explanation.walkthrough: '8s' refers to the answer to 8-down, KITCHEN; the second sense is the basins found in kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: To descend below the surface is to founder; washing-up basins are fixtures of a kitchen.

clue.text: Do playboys become such decent chaps ?

definitions.text: Do playboys become such decent chaps ?

parts.words: Do playboys become such decent chaps ?
parts.note: a playboy plays games, so might turn into one who plays fair, a good sport

explanation.surface: Asking whether pleasure-seekers grow up into gentlemen.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means both those who play sports and men who behave fairly.
explanation.definitionFit: Players of games, and men who play fair and behave decently.

clue.text: A little fellow has affinity for a little drink

parts.note: a nipper is a small child, a little lad
kin are relations, those with family affinity

explanation.surface: A small boy is drawn to a tiny tipple.
explanation.walkthrough: A nipperkin is an old word for a small measure of liquor, about half a pint or less.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic term for a small measure of wine or spirits.

clue.text: At nap she's made a mess of the game

indicators.note: messing up the letters puts them in a new order

explanation.surface: A card player bungles her hand at the game of nap.
explanation.walkthrough: Nap is a card game, which makes 'the game' look like a card reference; it means birds shot for sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Game birds hunted for sport; game here is quarry, not play.

clue.text: "I don't get it ", as the uneducable might say

definitions.text: "I don't get it ", as the uneducable might say

parts.words: "I don't get it ", as the uneducable might say
parts.note: someone who cannot be taught might complain they never acquire what learning brings

explanation.surface: What a hopeless pupil says when baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get it' suggests understanding a joke; the uneducable person literally never gets learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning is what someone unteachable fails to acquire.

clue.text: Distribution of cod is sure to cause conversation

indicators.note: distributing the letters spreads them out into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Sharing out the fish is bound to get people talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distribution of' rearranges COD IS SURE; the OCR text had a stray word 'columns', absent from the printed page.
explanation.definitionFit: Discourse is talk or spoken exchange, a synonym for conversation.

clue.text: Hot time spent in Barking ?

parts.note: Barking is an east London district, but the barking here is canine: the hottest weeks of summer named after the Dog Star

explanation.surface: A heatwave in the east London district of Barking.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is an area of east London; the hot spell of high summer is named after Sirius, the Dog Star.
explanation.definitionFit: The hottest weeks of summer, when Sirius rises with the sun.

clue.text: People could be lucky, following mother

indicators.note: what follows 'mother' in the longer word is left once that front is dropped

parts.note: mascots are charms that may bring luck
ma is mother

explanation.surface: Folk may be fortunate if they take after their mum.
explanation.walkthrough: Lucky charms are MASCOTS; the part following MA (mother) is SCOTS, the people of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots are a nation, a people of northern Britain.

clue.text: He risks creating outcries

indicators.note: the letters are used to create a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A daredevil causes uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creating' rearranges HE RISKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrill screams, synonyms for loud outcries.

clue.text: Extent of a full-scale operation

parts.note: sounds like a large undertaking, but 'full-scale' is musical: the whole range of notes of a scale

explanation.surface: How far a major undertaking reaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Full-scale' looks like 'large', but the word originally meant the whole musical scale, hence a complete range.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an entire range, originally the full series of notes in music.

clue.text: Measure in more senses than one

definitions.text: Measure in more senses than one

parts.words: Measure in more senses than one
parts.note: a unit of length, and also the rhythmic measure of verse

explanation.surface: A unit with several meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of length and also the rhythmic pattern of poetry.

clue.text: A man of spirit.

parts.note: seems to praise a man's courage, but 'spirit' is whisky or gin: a man who makes liquor

explanation.surface: A courageous fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests pluck, but here it is strong drink.
explanation.definitionFit: One who makes whisky or gin is literally involved with spirits.

clue.text: Discourage this gent giving you a powder

indicators.note: the longer word minus the man named leaves what is offered to the solver

parts.note: detergent is washing powder
taken as written, a gentleman

explanation.surface: An unpleasant man puts you off by handing you a powder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' plus GENT makes DETERGENT, a washing powder, so the answer is that powder without GENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone off, to dissuade.

clue.text: Conclude there's no getting away from. Hades

indicators.note: the little word escapes from the longer one, leaving it behind

parts.note: the inferno is hell, the underworld
taken as written

explanation.surface: Deciding that nobody escapes the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: Hades (the underworld) is INFERNO; NO gets away from it.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduce or reason out a conclusion.

clue.text: A man out to become mechanized:

definitions.text: A man out to become mechanized

indicators.note: the letters turn into something else, being rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Someone set on turning into a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'become' rearranges A MAN OUT TO, and the whole clue describes a man turned robot.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot is a man made mechanical, a self-operating machine.

clue.text: Nonsense can be sweet

definitions.meaning: as an exclamation, rubbish or humbug
a soft confection made of sugar, butter and milk

explanation.surface: Nonsense can still be charming.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an exclamation of disbelief and a soft sugary confection.

clue.text: Comparatively. strict, or backward 'on board'?

definitions.meaning: more severe, the comparative of stern
on a ship, further aft, closer to the rear end

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone strict or merely slow on a committee.
explanation.walkthrough: On a ship the stern is the back, so a sterner position is further aft.
explanation.definitionFit: More severe is the comparative of stern; aboard ship, further toward the back is nearer the stern.

clue.text: Men of letters — anagram experts?

definitions.meaning: post office workers who sort the mail
solvers who sort letters into new orders

explanation.surface: Writers who excel at word puzzles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men of letters' suggests writers, but here postal workers; anagrammers likewise sort letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Postal workers who arrange mail, and anyone who rearranges letters, both do this job.
